_comment: Third-party notices for PAM's local memory server, rendered by GET /notices (server/memory_app.py).
Source of truth: docs/LICENSES.md (the licence register, section 8 'notices-expected'); this file is derived.
scripts/check_notices.py compares the two both ways and exits 1 on drift; never edit one without the other.
Entry keys: component, version, licence (SPDX), source_url (primary source), notice_text (the copyright line,
the licence text and every required sentence, reproduced from hash-verified primary texts or the pinned wheel),
condition (always | provisioned:hand | provisioned:identity | calibration:cute | served:tabler): the page renders
an entry in full only while its condition holds on this server, and says so for the optional ones.
Builder B, 2026-10-10. Texts and hashes: docs/LICENSES.md section 7.

components.notice_text:
@mediapipe/tasks-vision 1.0.1: the hand-landmark runtime served from this origin when it is provisioned (vision_bundle.mjs, vision_wasm_internal.js, vision_wasm_internal.wasm, vision_wasm_nosimd_internal.js, vision_wasm_nosimd_internal.wasm). Optional component, fetched by the operator with scripts/fetch_models.py.

Copyright 2022 The MediaPipe Authors.
Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0.

The npm package ships no LICENSE or NOTICE file; the licence text below is the MediaPipe repository LICENSE (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/google-ai-edge/mediapipe/master/LICENSE). The repository has no NOTICE file, so nothing further is owed under section 4(d) of the licence.

Privacy disclosure (an obligation from the package README, not a licence term): The MediaPipe runtime contains a metrics logger that attempts to send usage statistics to Google (odml.pa.googleapis.com). PAM's Content-Security-Policy (connect-src 'self') blocks that request, so no metrics leave this origin. Google's notice: 'You are responsible for obtaining informed consent from your app users about Google's processing of MediaPipe metrics data as required by applicable law.'

Why Three Licenses?
===================

The zlib License could have been used instead of the Modified (3-clause) BSD
License, and since the IJG License effectively subsumes the distribution
conditions of the zlib License, this would have effectively placed
libjpeg-turbo binary distributions under the IJG License.  However, the IJG

attribution and endorsement protections to other entities.  Thus, it was
desirable to choose a license that granted us the same protections for new code
